According to the latest report from Bloomberg, Apple will launch a brand-new "Apple Upgrade" leasing plan in the United States at the end of this month. The report pointed out that this move marks "one of the largest changes in the company's history in how it sells equipment."

Here's how the plan works.

Lower monthly fees for hardware purchases

Apple has partnered with Klarna to support the new Apple Upgrade plan. Consumers will need to undergo a soft credit check when applying.

According to reports, Apple Upgrade will operate "like a subscription service" and apply to purchases of iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Apple Watch. However, the plan has certain restrictions. The report noted that Apple Watch SE, the basic iPad, iPhone 16, and MacBook Neo are not covered by Apple Upgrade.

According to reports, the lease term for iPhone and Apple Watch is 24 months, while the lease term for Mac is 36 months.

Mark Gurman explains as follows:

Unlike the iPhone Upgrade Program, Apple Upgrade does not include AppleCare services. In fact, Bloomberg reported that Apple plans to stop accepting new registrations for the iPhone Upgrade Program with the launch of Apple Upgrade.

According to reports, Apple Upgrade will officially launch on July 28, one week from today.

Apple raised the prices of iPad and Mac last month, and the new iPhone expected to launch in September is also expected to see further price increases. Apple Upgrade will offer consumers a solution to cope with rising prices, allowing them to choose as they wish.
